source_evidence.fullclaim:
Input nonsingular real $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, exact data $b\in\mathbb R^n$, and an initial iterate $x_0$ stored at solve/update precision $u_w$. Also input stored triangular factors $\widehat L,\widehat U$ formed at factorization precision $u_f$, where $\widehat L$ is lower triangular, $\widehat U$ is upper triangular, both have nonzero diagonals, and $\widehat A:=\widehat L\widehat U$ is the exact real product; thus $\widehat A$ is nonsingular. Input residual precision $u_r$, solve/update precision $u_w$, finite update budget $N\ge0$, tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a stagnation window $K_{\rm stag}\ge1$, nonnegative constants $\eta_r,\xi_r,\eta_w,\xi_w$, and a proposed contraction upper bound $0\le q_{\rm cert}<1$. Let $x_*=A^{-1}b$. Use the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] at each stated precision. Entries of the exact data $A,b$ are available as real operands to the residual operations; the stored factors, iterates, residuals, and corrections are used as their exact represented values in those operations.

Certificates have the following fixed format: one real matrix $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ before iteration, nonnegative real scalars $\rho_k$ for $0\le k\le N$, and nonnegative real scalars $\omega_k$ for $0\le k<N$. Each entry may instead be marked missing. All certificate checks use exact real addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a positive number, nonnegative square roots, and comparisons; they are not rounded operations at $u_r$ or $u_w$. Evaluate finite sums and products in increasing index order. In particular, evaluate $\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i v_i^2}$ and $\|M\|_F=\sqrt{\sum_{i,j}M_{ij}^2}$ by these exact operations. This is an ideal exact-real certificate verifier, not a claim that arbitrary real inputs admit a finite-bit implementation.

Before iterating, check triangularity and nonzero diagonals of the factors; on failure return `inconclusive` with $x_0$. A missing or incorrectly shaped $B$ returns `inconclusive` with $x_0$. Form $\widehat A=\widehat L\widehat U$ exactly and check $B\widehat A=I$ entrywise. If this fails, return `inconclusive` with $x_0$. Set
$$a_+=\|A\|_F,\qquad a_-=a_+/\sqrt n,\qquad h=\|B\|_F,\qquad d=\|I-BA\|_F.$$
Accept the initial certificate precisely when
$$d+h\bigl((1+\eta_w)\eta_r+\eta_w\bigr)a_+\le q_{\rm cert}<1;$$
otherwise return `inconclusive` with $x_0$. Here $B=\widehat A^{-1}$, and the inequalities $a_-\le\|A\|_2\le a_+$ and $\|M\|_2\le\|M\|_F$ from [[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]] make this a sufficient certificate for
$$q=\|I-\widehat A^{-1}A\|_2+\|\widehat A^{-1}\|_2\bigl((1+\eta_w)\eta_r+\eta_w\bigr)\|A\|_2\le q_{\rm cert}.$$
These conservative tests may reject data for which sharper norm certificates exist.

Before entering the iteration loop, initialize the consecutive-equality counter $c_{\rm stag}=0$ and mark the preceding residual as undefined. Retain this counter and preceding residual across iterations; do not reinitialize them inside the loop. The counter records the number of consecutive equalities between adjacent successfully certified computed residual vectors.

For each $k=0,\ldots,N$, compute the residual by rows in increasing $i$: initialize $s_i=0$, then for $j=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order compute $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(A_{ij}x_{k,j})$ and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(s_i+p_{ij})$; finally set $\widehat r_{k,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(b_i-s_i)$. Any operationwise range failure returns `inconclusive` with the current iterate and the first failing row, column, and operation. Define the exact residual defect $\delta_{r,k}=\widehat r_k-(b-Ax_k)$, so $\widehat r_k=A(x_*-x_k)+\delta_{r,k}$. Check that $\rho_k$ is present and nonnegative and that
$$\sum_i\delta_{r,k,i}^2\le\rho_k^2,\qquad \rho_k\le\eta_r(a_-\|x_k\|_2+\|b\|_2)+\xi_r.$$
A missing scalar or failed comparison returns `inconclusive` with the current iterate. These exact tests imply $\|\delta_{r,k}\|_2\le\eta_r(\|A\|_2\|x_k\|_2+\|b\|_2)+\xi_r$.
Use the retained consecutive-equality counter and preceding residual. Use the exact Euclidean norm of the stored residual vector for the status comparison; this is a comparison of the already computed vector, not an additional rounded arithmetic operation. If $\|\widehat r_k\|_2\le\tau$, return `residual-tolerance` with $x_k$. If a preceding residual exists, compare its components exactly with those of $\widehat r_k$: if all are equal, increment $c_{\rm stag}$ by one; otherwise reset it to zero. If $c_{\rm stag}=K_{\rm stag}$, return `successful-stagnation` with $x_k$. This status certifies only that the last $K_{\rm stag}$ successful updates produced identical computed residual vectors, with all range and contraction certificates accepted; it certifies neither a small exact error nor convergence. Before any further update, store $\widehat r_k$ as the preceding residual.

If $k=N$ and neither status above was returned, return `budget-exhausted` with $x_k$. Otherwise solve $\widehat L y_k=\widehat r_k$ by forward substitution, then $\widehat U\widehat z_k=y_k$ by backward substitution, using precision $u_w$. For forward substitution, visit rows $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, initialize $s_i=0$, and for $j=1,\ldots,i-1$ in increasing order compute $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(\widehat L_{ij}y_{k,j})$ and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(s_i+p_{ij})$, then $t_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(\widehat r_{k,i}-s_i)$ and $y_{k,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(t_i/\widehat L_{ii})$. For backward substitution, visit rows $i=n,\ldots,1$ in decreasing order, initialize $s_i=0$, and for $j=i+1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order compute $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(\widehat U_{ij}\widehat z_{k,j})$ and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(s_i+p_{ij})$, then $t_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(y_{k,i}-s_i)$ and $\widehat z_{k,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(t_i/\widehat U_{ii})$. Update components in increasing order by $x_{k+1,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(x_{k,i}+\widehat z_{k,i})$. A failed operation returns `inconclusive` with the current iterate and first failing operation location.

After a successful update, define the exact residual-equivalent update defect
$$\delta_{w,k}:=\widehat A(x_{k+1}-x_k)-\widehat r_k,$$
so $x_{k+1}=x_k+\widehat A^{-1}(\widehat r_k+\delta_{w,k})$. Check that $\omega_k$ is present and nonnegative and that $\sum_i\delta_{w,k,i}^2\le\omega_k^2$ and $\omega_k\le\eta_w\|\widehat r_k\|_2+\xi_w$; otherwise return `inconclusive` with $x_{k+1}$. These tests imply $\|\delta_{w,k}\|_2\le\eta_w\|\widehat r_k\|_2+\xi_w$. Continue until one of the stated statuses is returned. All loops are finite. The procedure does not claim exact termination or unconditional convergence.

Also input stored triangular factors $\widehat L,\widehat U$ formed at factorization precision $u_f$, where $\widehat L$ is lower triangular, $\widehat U$ is upper triangular, both have nonzero diagonals, and $\widehat A:=\widehat L\widehat U$ is the exact real product; thus $\widehat A$ is nonsingular. Input residual precision $u_r$, solve/update precision $u_w$, finite update budget $N\ge0$, tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a stagnation window $K_{\rm stag}\ge1$, nonnegative constants $\eta_r,\xi_r,\eta_w,\xi_w$, and a proposed contraction upper bound $0\le q_{\rm cert}<1$. Let $x_*=A^{-1}b$. Use the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] at each stated precision. Entries of the exact data $A,b$ are available as real operands to the residual operations; the stored factors, iterates, residuals, and corrections are used as their exact represented values in those operations.

Certificates have the following fixed format: one real matrix $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ before iteration, nonnegative real scalars $\rho_k$ for $0\le k\le N$, and nonnegative real scalars $\omega_k$ for $0\le k<N$. Each entry may instead be marked missing. All certificate checks use exact real addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a positive number, nonnegative square roots, and comparisons; they are not rounded operations at $u_r$ or $u_w$. Evaluate finite sums and products in increasing index order. In particular, evaluate $\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i v_i^2}$ and $\|M\|_F=\sqrt{\sum_{i,j}M_{ij}^2}$ by these exact operations. This is an ideal exact-real certificate verifier, not a claim that arbitrary real inputs admit a finite-bit implementation.

Before iterating, check triangularity and nonzero diagonals of the factors; on failure return `inconclusive` with $x_0$. A missing or incorrectly shaped $B$ returns `inconclusive` with $x_0$. Form $\widehat A=\widehat L\widehat U$ exactly and check $B\widehat A=I$ entrywise. If this fails, return `inconclusive` with $x_0$. Set
$$a_+=\|A\|_F,\qquad a_-=a_+/\sqrt n,\qquad h=\|B\|_F,\qquad d=\|I-BA\|_F.$$
Accept the initial certificate precisely when
$$d+h\bigl((1+\eta_w)\eta_r+\eta_w\bigr)a_+\le q_{\rm cert}<1;$$
otherwise return `inconclusive` with $x_0$. Here $B=\widehat A^{-1}$, and the inequalities $a_-\le\|A\|_2\le a_+$ and $\|M\|_2\le\|M\|_F$ from [[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]] make this a sufficient certificate for
$$q=\|I-\widehat A^{-1}A\|_2+\|\widehat A^{-1}\|_2\bigl((1+\eta_w)\eta_r+\eta_w\bigr)\|A\|_2\le q_{\rm cert}.$$
These conservative tests may reject data for which sharper norm certificates exist.

Before entering the iteration loop, initialize the consecutive-equality counter $c_{\rm stag}=0$ and mark the preceding residual as undefined. Retain this counter and preceding residual across iterations; do not reinitialize them inside the loop. The counter records the number of consecutive equalities between adjacent successfully certified computed residual vectors.

For each $k=0,\ldots,N$, compute the residual by rows in increasing $i$: initialize $s_i=0$, then for $j=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order compute $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(A_{ij}x_{k,j})$ and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(s_i+p_{ij})$; finally set $\widehat r_{k,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(b_i-s_i)$. Any operationwise range failure returns `inconclusive` with the current iterate and the first failing row, column, and operation. Define the exact residual defect $\delta_{r,k}=\widehat r_k-(b-Ax_k)$, so $\widehat r_k=A(x_*-x_k)+\delta_{r,k}$. Check that $\rho_k$ is present and nonnegative and that
$$\sum_i\delta_{r,k,i}^2\le\rho_k^2,\qquad \rho_k\le\eta_r(a_-\|x_k\|_2+\|b\|_2)+\xi_r.$$
A missing scalar or failed comparison returns `inconclusive` with the current iterate. These exact tests imply $\|\delta_{r,k}\|_2\le\eta_r(\|A\|_2\|x_k\|_2+\|b\|_2)+\xi_r$.
Use the retained consecutive-equality counter and preceding residual. Use the exact Euclidean norm of the stored residual vector for the status comparison; this is a comparison of the already computed vector, not an additional rounded arithmetic operation. If $\|\widehat r_k\|_2\le\tau$, return `residual-tolerance` with $x_k$. If a preceding residual exists, compare its components exactly with those of $\widehat r_k$: if all are equal, increment $c_{\rm stag}$ by one; otherwise reset it to zero. If $c_{\rm stag}=K_{\rm stag}$, return `successful-stagnation` with $x_k$. This status certifies only that the last $K_{\rm stag}$ successful updates produced identical computed residual vectors, with all range and contraction certificates accepted; it certifies neither a small exact error nor convergence. Before any further update, store $\widehat r_k$ as the preceding residual.

If $k=N$ and neither status above was returned, return `budget-exhausted` with $x_k$. Otherwise solve $\widehat L y_k=\widehat r_k$ by forward substitution, then $\widehat U\widehat z_k=y_k$ by backward substitution, using precision $u_w$. For forward substitution, visit rows $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, initialize $s_i=0$, and for $j=1,\ldots,i-1$ in increasing order compute $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(\widehat L_{ij}y_{k,j})$ and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(s_i+p_{ij})$, then $t_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(\widehat r_{k,i}-s_i)$ and $y_{k,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(t_i/\widehat L_{ii})$. For backward substitution, visit rows $i=n,\ldots,1$ in decreasing order, initialize $s_i=0$, and for $j=i+1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order compute $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(\widehat U_{ij}\widehat z_{k,j})$ and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(s_i+p_{ij})$, then $t_i=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(y_{k,i}-s_i)$ and $\widehat z_{k,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(t_i/\widehat U_{ii})$. Update components in increasing order by $x_{k+1,i}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(x_{k,i}+\widehat z_{k,i})$. A failed operation returns `inconclusive` with the current iterate and first failing operation location.

After a successful update, define the exact residual-equivalent update defect
$$\delta_{w,k}:=\widehat A(x_{k+1}-x_k)-\widehat r_k,$$
so $x_{k+1}=x_k+\widehat A^{-1}(\widehat r_k+\delta_{w,k})$. Check that $\omega_k$ is present and nonnegative and that $\sum_i\delta_{w,k,i}^2\le\omega_k^2$ and $\omega_k\le\eta_w\|\widehat r_k\|_2+\xi_w$; otherwise return `inconclusive` with $x_{k+1}$. These tests imply $\|\delta_{w,k}\|_2\le\eta_w\|\widehat r_k\|_2+\xi_w$. Continue until one of the stated statuses is returned. All loops are finite. The procedure does not claim exact termination or unconditional convergence.

$$A_J(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{J}\frac{(-1)^jt^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad R_J(t)=\frac{|t|^{2J+3}}{(2J+3)(1-t^2)}.$$
The Machin identity gives the interval $P=16I_J(1/5)-4I_J(1/239)$ containing $\pi$. Form the exact rational interval $qP$ by taking the minimum and maximum of its two endpoint products, then round its endpoints down and up to obtain a dyadic input interval $\Theta$ in format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$. If this conversion overflows, treat that precision as a non-finite evaluation. Otherwise build two finite real expression DAGs with input interval $\Theta$ and requested outputs $\cos(\Theta)$ and $\sin(\Theta)$, and call [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] using the same dyadic format and truncation index $J$; its fixed finite-cell rules govern range reduction. If either result is non-finite, continue at the next precision unless the precision cap is reached, in which case return `inconclusive` with the supplier status. If the results are finite intervals $C=[c_-,c_+]$ and $S=[s_-,s_+]$, set $\widehat w=c_-+is_-$ and compute an upward-rounded dyadic $\epsilon\ge(c_+-c_-)+(s_+-s_-)$. If $\epsilon\le\tau$, return `certified(\widehat w,\epsilon)`; otherwise continue or return `inconclusive` at the cap. A non-finite endpoint or overflow returns its explicit failure status. The routine makes no finite-error claim on a failure branch.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
**Inputs.** A finite state reaction system
[[def-reaction-network-propensity-system-and-generator]] with nonzero jump
vectors, initial state $x_0\in E$, horizon $T>0$, maximum leap
$\tau_{\max}>0$, critical threshold $n_c\in\mathbb N$, finite step budget
$B$ that is a nonnegative integer, and independent ideal random inputs for
the procedure. Use a fresh independent direct-method stream on every critical
SSA call. Also use mutually independent unit-uniform streams
$U_{q,j,r}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$, independent of all SSA streams, for
leap indices $q$, channels $j$, and positive trial indices $r=1,2,\ldots$. A
binomial draw with parameters $(m_j,p_j)$ is the number of the first $m_j$
entries in its stream that are less than $p_j$. The countable product of these input laws
exists under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice by
[[thm-countable-product-of-probability-spaces]]. The first-event law of the
critical SSA subroutine is the one in
[[thm-finite-state-gillespie-and-next-reaction-exactness]]. For a state $x$
and channel $j$, define its admissible firing
capacity
$$\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\},\qquad m_j(x):=\max\{m\in\mathbb N_0:x+r\nu_j\in E \text{ for every integer }r\in\{0,\ldots,m\}\}.$$
Finiteness of $E$ and $\nu_j\ne0$ make this maximum finite. Let
$C(x)=\{j:m_j(x)\le n_c\}$ be the critical set. When $C(x)\ne\varnothing$,
hold $C(x)$ fixed and form the finite reaction system on $E$ using only those
channels, with their original propensities. If $C(x)=\varnothing$, do not
form a restricted system and define the critical result to be no event. In
the nonempty case, the critical SSA subroutine runs the direct Gillespie
method on this restricted system with event budget one and horizon $\tau$;
it returns its first event $(s,j_*)$ if it occurs strictly before $\tau$,
where $0<s<\tau$, and otherwise returns no event.

**Output.** The recorded states at accepted leap endpoints, with
piecewise-constant interpolation, and a status in {**completed**,
**absorbed**, **invalid-state**, **inconclusive**,
**step-size-infeasible**, **critical-interface-required**}. A noncompleted
step-size, interface, or budget failure returns the current path prefix.
Absorption and invalid-state handling record the held state through $T$.

**Procedure.** Set $t=0$, $x=x_0$, step counter $q=0$,
recorded path $P=[(0,x_0)]$, and status **completed**.

1. If $t=T$, return $P$ with status **completed**. If $x\notin E$, append
   $(t,x)$ to $P$ if needed, append $(T,x)$ if $t<T$, and return $P$ with
   status **invalid-state**. If $q=B$ before $T$, return the current path
   prefix with status **inconclusive**. If $\lambda(x)=0$, hold
   $x$ fixed through $T$, append $(T,x)$ to $P$ if needed, and return $P$
   with status **absorbed**.
2. Compute $C(x)$ and
   $$\tau=\min\!\left(T-t,\tau_{\max}, \min_{\substack{j\notin C(x)\\a_j(x)>0}}\frac{m_j(x)}{a_j(x)}\right),$$
   where the inner minimum over an empty set is $+\infty$. If $\tau\le0$,
   return **step-size-infeasible** with the current path prefix. If
   $C(x)=\varnothing$, record that there is no critical event and skip
   the critical SSA call. If $C(x)\ne\varnothing$, call critical SSA for
   horizon $\tau$; it returns either no critical event before $\tau$, or a
   pair $(s,j_*)$ with $0<s<\tau$ and $j_*\in C(x)$.
   Set $\delta$ to $s$ in the event case and to $\tau$ otherwise.
3. Starting from $\widetilde x=x$, process the noncritical channels in
   increasing index order. Recompute $m_j(\widetilde x)$. If $a_j(\widetilde x)>0$ and
   $m_j(\widetilde x)=0$, return **critical-interface-required** with the
   current path prefix. Otherwise
   set $K_j=0$ when $m_j(\widetilde x)=0=a_j(\widetilde x)$. When
   $m_j(\widetilde x)>0$, set
   $p_j=a_j(\widetilde x)\delta/m_j(\widetilde x)$; if $p_j>1$, return
   **step-size-infeasible** with the current path prefix and without rejecting
   and resampling. Set
   $$K_j=\sum_{r=1}^{m_j(\widetilde x)}\mathbf 1_{\{U_{q,j,r}<p_j\}},\qquad
   \widetilde x\leftarrow\widetilde x+K_j\nu_j.$$
4. If critical SSA returned $(s,j_*)$, return **inconclusive** with the
   current path prefix when $\widetilde x+\nu_{j_*}\notin E$; otherwise apply
   that critical reaction to $\widetilde x$. If the call returned no event,
   leave $\widetilde x$ unchanged. Set $x\leftarrow\widetilde x$, set
   $t\leftarrow t+\delta$, append $(t,x)$ to $P$, set $q\leftarrow q+1$,
   and repeat.

This supremum is a finite real: if $B=(b_{ij})$ in the standard basis, then for $\|z\|_\infty=1$,

$$\|x_*-x_0\|_\infty\le2\beta\|F(x_0)\|_\infty.$$

[F9] [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]: for the composition $y\mapsto A^{-1}F(y)$, its derivative is $A^{-1}DF(y)$.
complete_sections.Proof:
**Proof technique:** contraction.

1.1 Define $\Phi(y):=y-A^{-1}F(y)$ on $B_\infty(x_0,2r)$. By [F1] and [F9], $D\Phi(y)=I-A^{-1}DF(y)=A^{-1}(A-DF(y))$. The induced maximum norm is submultiplicative directly from its definition, and [F8] ensures it is well-defined, so for $y\in\overline B_\infty(x_0,r)$ the Lipschitz hypothesis gives $\|D\Phi(y)\|_\infty\le\beta L\|y-x_0\|_\infty\le\beta Lr\le\tfrac12$. [F1, F2, F8, F9, given, algebra]

1.2 Let $(x^{(m)})$ be Cauchy in $d_\infty$. For every $j<n$, $|x^{(m)}_j-x^{(l)}_j|\le d_\infty(x^{(m)},x^{(l)})$, so the $j$th coordinate sequence is Cauchy in $\mathbb R$ and converges to some $y_j$ by [F4]. The finitely many unique limits define $y\in\mathbb R^n$. Given $\delta>0$, choose for each $j<n$ an index $K_j$ such that $|x^{(m)}_j-y_j|<\delta$ for $m\ge K_j$; since $n\ge1$, [F7] gives $K=\max_{j<n}K_j$. Then $d_\infty(x^{(m)},y)<\delta$ for $m\ge K$. Thus $(\mathbb R^n,d_\infty)$ is complete. [F4, F7, given, choose]

2.1 For any $y,z$ in the closed radius-$r$ ball, their joining segment lies in the open radius-$2r$ ball. For each coordinate $j$, the scalar function $t\mapsto\Phi_j(z+t(y-z))$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and differentiable on $(0,1)$ by [F1] and [F9]. Its derivative has absolute value at most $\|D\Phi(z+t(y-z))\|_\infty\|y-z\|_\infty\le\tfrac12\|y-z\|_\infty$. Applying [F3] coordinatewise and taking the maximum gives $\|\Phi(y)-\Phi(z)\|_\infty\le\tfrac12\|y-z\|_\infty$. [F1, F3, F9, step 1.1, given]

3.1 At the center, $\|\Phi(x_0)-x_0\|_\infty=\|A^{-1}F(x_0)\|_\infty\le\beta\epsilon\le r/2$. Thus for $y$ in the closed ball, step 2.1 gives $\|\Phi(y)-x_0\|_\infty\le\|\Phi(y)-\Phi(x_0)\|_\infty+\|\Phi(x_0)-x_0\|_\infty\le r/2+r/2=r$, so $\Phi$ maps the ball into itself. [F2, given, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The closed ball is nonempty and complete by step 1.2 and [F5]. Hence [F6] gives a unique fixed point $x_*\in\overline B_\infty(x_0,r)$. Its fixed-point equation gives $A^{-1}F(x_*)=0$, and invertibility in [F2] yields $F(x_*)=0$. [F2, F5, F6, step 3.1, step 1.2]

5.1 By step 2.1, $\|\Phi(x_*)-\Phi(x_0)\|_\infty\le\tfrac12\|x_*-x_0\|_\infty$. The fixed-point identity $\Phi(x_*)=x_*$ and the center estimate in step 3.1 therefore give $\|x_*-x_0\|_\infty\le\tfrac12\|x_*-x_0\|_\infty+\beta\epsilon$, hence $\|x_*-x_0\|_\infty\le2\beta\epsilon$. Any zero in the ball is a fixed point of $\Phi$, hence equals $x_*$. [F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded polyhedral open control domain, and let $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ be a family of matching affine simplicial meshes of $E$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. $$
(\Pi_hq)|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kq.
$$
Then $\Pi_h$ is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection onto the cellwise-constant space. For every $q\in H^1(E)$,
$$
\|q-\Pi_hq\|_{L^2(E)}\le C h\,|q|_{H^1(E)},

$$

$$
Then $\Pi_h$ is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection onto the cellwise-constant space. For every $q\in H^1(E)$,
$$

$$

complete_sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** Countable Choice; the affine simplex mesh convention; $q\in L^2(E)$ for orthogonal projection and $q\in H^1(E)$ for the error estimate; and, only for box preservation, cellwise-constant bounds with $q_a\le q\le q_b$ almost everywhere.

[F1] A cell map is an affine bijection from the fixed reference simplex, and the cells have disjoint interiors ([[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]).

[F2] Affine pullback transports weak derivatives and Sobolev seminorms by the matrix and determinant factors ([[lem-affine-pullback-weak-derivatives-and-scaling]]).

[F3] On the reference simplex, subtracting the cell mean leaves an $L^2$ norm bounded by a constant times the $H^1$ seminorm ([[thm-reference-simplex-poincare-wirtinger]]).

[F4] Hölder with exponents $2,2$ makes each $L^2(K)$ function integrable on the finite-measure cell, so its mean is finite ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]).

[F5] Change of variables holds for nonnegative measurable integrands; applying it to the positive and negative parts gives the formula for the integrable real function $q$ ([[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]).

[F6] Every mesh facet lies in a Lebesgue-null affine hyperplane, so the finite union of facets is null ([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]).

[A1] Countable Choice is the stated hypothesis of [F2] and [F3] ([[def-countable-choice]]).
complete_sections.Proof:
1.1 By [F4], the cell means are finite, and finitely many finite cell values define an element of the cellwise-constant subspace of $L^2(E)$. For every cellwise-constant $c$, $\int_K(q-\Pi_hq)c|_K=0$ by the mean identity. Summing over cells, ignoring the null facets by [F6], gives $(q-\Pi_hq,c)_U=0$, proving the orthogonal-projection property for all $q\in L^2(E)$. If additionally $q_a|_K\le q\le q_b|_K$, integration and division by $|K|>0$ place each mean in that interval; hence $\Pi_hq\in Q_{ad}$. [F1, F4, F6, given, algebra]

1.2 Fix a cell $K$ with affine map $F_K(\hat x)=b_K+A_K\hat x$ and write $\hat q=q\circ F_K$. By [F5], change of variables applied to $q^+$ and $q^-$ gives the signed integral formula; [F6] lets us ignore the cell facets. Hence $(\Pi_hq)|_K\circ F_K=\hat q_{\widehat S_d}$, the mean of $\hat q$ on the reference simplex. By [F3], $\|q-\Pi_hq\|_{L^2(K)} =|\det A_K|^{1/2}\|\hat q-\hat q_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^2(\widehat S_d)} \le C|\det A_K|^{1/2}|\hat q|_{H^1(\widehat S_d)}.$ By [F2], $|\hat q|_{H^1(\widehat S_d)}\le C\|A_K\||\det A_K|^{-1/2}|q|_{H^1(K)}$, and $\|A_K\|\le C_d h_K$ from the fixed reference simplex geometry. Thus $\|q-\Pi_hq\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K|q|_{H^1(K)}$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 Square the cell estimates in step 1.2 and sum over cells; the interiors are disjoint and their omitted facets are null by [F6]. Since $h_K\le h$, the sum is at most $C^2h^2|q|_{H^1(E)}^2$. Taking square roots proves the global bound. [F1, F6, step 1.2, algebra] ∎
